title: Prime Important Meetings With Prework
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that consequential meetings shouldn't begin when people walk into the room but rather the moment the invitation is sent. Well-designed prework, reading, summarizing, or clarifying material ahead of time, creates a common foundation so the actual meeting time can be spent on discussion rather than first exposure to the issues. The author acknowledges that teams often abandon prework when members resist doing it, but argues the fix is treating prework as the literal price of admission: no prework, no seat at the table. Once teams experience the payoff in meeting quality, the practice sells itself.
points: Important meetings should be primed with prework starting the moment the invitation goes out.
Prework should engage and challenge people, not amount to busywork.
Teams often abandon prework requirements when members resist, missing out on its benefits.
Treating prework as a requirement for attendance dramatically increases compliance.
Meetings become far more productive once participants arrive already immersed in the material.
quotes: Important meetings, where decisions are made and strategies set, need to be primed for success.
In the ideal design, the meeting starts the moment the invitation goes out and the calendar is set.
Prework is never busy work. It should be designed to get the juices and ideas flowing.
Leaders detest herding people who resist and say they are too busy, so they often hit the eject button and give up on what they know would be a highly additive exercise.
On better teams, the prework is the entry ticket to attend the meeting, no matter who you are or what status you hold on the team.
True meeting success occurs when preparation meets discussion.
